question: Biologists paint-marked every worker in lab colonies of Temnothorax ants. Roughly what share turned out to be inactive most of the time?
answer: About two in five. Charbonneau and Dornhaus followed individually marked ants and found a large, consistent group that rarely worked. Later removal experiments suggest they are partly a reserve: take away the busiest workers and some idle ones step in. The ants on a trail are the busy ones; the idle wait in the dark.
move: The members seen working were chosen, in part, by being seen.
ask: Whose work do I judge by the busy people I see, while ignoring those I never see?
trap: Judging a colony by its foragers, the only ants anyone watches.
source: Charbonneau & Dornhaus, Behavioral Ecology and Sociobiology, 2015
reference: Charbonneau & Dornhaus, Workers 'specialized' on inactivity: behavioral consistency of inactive workers and their role in task allocation, Behavioral Ecology and Sociobiology, 2015
